sources.dataset: World Urbanization Prospects 2025 Revision - Degree of Urbanization
sources.coverage: Annual population 1950-2050; land and built-up area 1975-2050
sources.unit: country or area by internationally harmonized settlement category
sources.role: National urbanization-stage controls; not an individual-city panel
sources.citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2025). World Urbanization Prospects: The 2025 Revision, Online Edition.
sources.notes: F01-F04 are country/category tables. They cannot support individual-city hypotheses. Register exact downloads rather than assuming legacy table names.

sources.coverage: Annual estimates through 2025 and projections through 2050 for more than 12,000 cities with at least 50,000 inhabitants in 2025; area series begin in 1975
sources.unit: individual internationally harmonized city or urban settlement
sources.role: Primary city-level population, surface-area, density and growth panel
sources.citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2025). World Urbanization Prospects: The 2025 Revision, Online Edition.
sources.notes: F21 contains cities that reach 50,000 during 1975-2050, but annual values are blank while a city is below 50,000. This is time-varying threshold truncation, not a balanced history and not selection only at 2025. Keep estimates and projections distinct.

sources.unit: DEGURBA urban centre; fixed-2025 and multi-temporal boundary streams
sources.role: Spatial footprint, density, area-change, geometry and boundary sensitivity
sources.citation: European Commission, Joint Research Centre. GHS Urban Centre Database 2024, R2024A.

files.boundary_semantics: statistics for all epochs inside the fixed 2025 urban-centre boundary
separate multi-temporal boundaries; values are not comparable with the fixed stream except at 2025

sources.notes: The v1.2 package readme explicitly replaces deprecated v1.1, despite the landing page still showing v1.1. Do not describe UCDB as an independent replication of WUP 2025; both depend on GHSL/DEGURBA. Fixed and dynamic values are different and not comparable except at 2025.

sources.role: National demographic controls and forecast baselines
sources.citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024.
sources.notes: Use vintages available at each historical forecast origin when testing genuine real-time forecasts; the current revision is revised-history evidence.

sources.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.dataset: OECD Cities and Functional Urban Areas
sources.coverage: OECD FUAs and worldwide estimated FUAs where published
sources.citation: OECD. Cities and Functional Urban Areas database.
sources.notes: Not globally interchangeable with GHSL urban centres; use on its supported sample as a mechanism test.

sources.citation: WorldPop, University of Southampton. Global high-resolution population estimates.
sources.notes: Top-down estimates are adjusted to national totals and are too short for the primary 1975-forward persistence analysis.

sources.role: Upstream DEGURBA delineation dependency for WUP 2025 and UCDB
sources.citation: European Commission, Joint Research Centre. GHS-SMOD R2023A.
sources.notes: Registering this upstream product makes the WUP/UCDB methodological dependence explicit; it is not automatically required as a local analytical input.

sources.coverage: Global country boundaries and island geometries
sources.notes: Political-status and boundary choices must be documented; map geometry is not a migration-policy measure.
